sentences.text: The Pharmacy Verification Station serves as the final controlled checkpoint before a medication is made available for dispensing.
The Clinical Pharmacist compares the active medication order with the product, strength, dosage form, dose, route, and scheduled time.
The Clinical Pharmacist also confirms that the patient identifiers and pharmacy label agree with the authorized order.
The Pharmacy Technician checks package integrity, lot identification, and expiry before presenting the medication for verification.
For designated high-risk medications, an independent second check is completed and recorded before authorization.
Any mismatch places the medication on hold until the discrepancy is resolved by an authorized pharmacy professional.
The verification record captures the approving staff identity, time, and medication identifiers for later review.
The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot remains inhibited from completing a dispense until the required pharmacy authorization is present.
The Clinical Pharmacist resolves unclear or conflicting order details through the Medication Order Gateway before authorizing release.
The South Ward Cabinet Controller receives the release note and applies its own approved cabinet configuration before enabling any compartment.
The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks its local compartment mapping, access rules, and supported medication classes against that configuration.
The cabinet reports Ready for Dispense only after its configuration checks and required device self-tests pass.
The Registered Nurse authenticates at the cabinet and selects the medication associated with the active patient order.
The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks the requested selection against its local authorization rules before unlocking a compartment.
The cabinet records the user, order reference, compartment access, and transaction time for audit review.
Stonewake reviews the received operational record, correlates its equipment identifiers and timestamps with local telemetry, and records an engineering disposition.
The Biomedical Engineer uses the exception ticket to identify the affected path and compare reported symptoms with equipment telemetry.
The Biomedical Engineer checks whether the reported condition is isolated to one device or indicates a broader service risk.
When a hardware or control fault is suspected, the affected equipment is placed in Out of Service status.
The Biomedical Engineer isolates the affected subsystem and performs only the diagnostic steps approved for that equipment.
The IT Operations Specialist investigates authentication, interface, and time-synchronization faults that could affect transaction records.
The Medication Safety Officer reviews any discrepancy that could change medication identity, access control, or patient risk.
The Clinical Pharmacist keeps affected medication unavailable until the relevant order and product checks are repeated successfully.
The Biomedical Engineer records the corrective action, test evidence, and approvals required to return the equipment to operation.
Equipment remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return.
Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.
